import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';

// Read the known audit file — the second test-assertion channel alongside the UI. The app appends
// one record per line; specs filter it by their sheet id. Path comes from AUDIT_FILE (set by
// bin/start / bin/e2e); falls back to the app's default.
const AUDIT_FILE = process.env.AUDIT_FILE ?? '../.run/audit.log';

/** All audit records currently in the file, one per element (empty if none). */
export function auditLines(): string[] {
  return existsSync(AUDIT_FILE)
    ? readFileSync(AUDIT_FILE, 'utf8').split('\n').filter((l) => l.length > 0)
    : [];
}

// Usage in a spec (audit-category test):
//   expect(auditLines()).toContain('OWNER_CREATED id=1 name=Acme');
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid

# Spring Boot host config. H2 in-memory in the same JVM; Flyway migrates the schema up on boot from
# db/migration; Actuator health is the readiness probe.

# In-memory H2 (dies with the JVM = clean per-run reset).
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:officehq;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=

# Flyway owns the schema. JPA does not create tables.
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
# Close the persistence context at the end of the request, not during view rendering.
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# Readiness probe.
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true

# The SPA is served from src/main/resources/static (built there by bin/build); deep-link
# fallback is in SpaConfig.java.

# Audit sink: one record per line to this known file, so tests assert side-effects by reading it.
# bin/start passes an absolute path via AUDIT_FILE; default is .run/audit.log.
app.audit.file=${AUDIT_FILE:.run/audit.log}

content.text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and the test passes when run with `bin/e2e`. The file contained exactly these four lines from that run; the refused claim and the duplicate "Ada" wrote nothing:

```
PERSON_ADDED sheet=… by=uma name=Ada grade=A
PERSON_EDITED sheet=… by=uma name=Ada grade=B
CLAIM_ADDED sheet=… by=uma person=Ada amount=5.00 date=2026-03-02
CLAIM_EDITED sheet=… by=uma person=Ada amount=6.00 date=2026-03-02
```

The changes are all on the server:

- **`Audit.java`**: a new `change(event, sheetId, user, fields...)` method builds the line in the required order. A line is written only after the database change has been saved. If a change is refused or fails at any point, now or under rules added later, it writes no line and saves nothing.
- **`PersonService` / `ClaimService`**: these now write `PERSON_ADDED`, `PERSON_EDITED`, `CLAIM_ADDED` and `CLAIM_EDITED`. Claim lines use the person's name, the amount with two decimals, and the date as yyyy-mm-dd.
- **`PersonController` / `ClaimController`**: the edit endpoints now pass on the signed-in user, which they already received but didn't use, so edit lines can fill in `by=`.

No front-end or database changes were needed.
